newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold eroding towards previous lows.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold eroding towards previous lows.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold looks to be in the process of unfolding a bearish flag pattern, heralding eventual tests of last week's $313.60 lows, dealers and analysts said.
Silver also is expected to break lower below the previous $4.23 floor, they added.
GOLD -
Prices were concluding a week-long sideways movement and should now move to probe last week's 12-year lows after failing to challenge $322/$323 per ounce resistance over the past few days.
"It is looking like a bear flag...it should retest and break below the $313.60 low," said chartist Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
Analyst Steve Porter of Elliott Wave International said $317 was a key level on the way down. "A break of $317.00 should see downside acceleration," he said in a commentary.
Analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff said the Comex August contract should test initial support at $314.50 while targeting $310.
Jones said there was not a lot of support for spot gold on the way down, pegging $312 and $309 as key levels. "The $300 level is not out of the ballpark," she added.
At 0735 GMT spot gold was quoted at $319.05/319.55, down 40 cents from Monday's New York close.
SILVER -
This market was also looking vulnerable after dropping below $4.30 on Monday.
"The downside is expected to remain under pressure," said Squires.
If the market violates last week's low of $4.23, prices would not be likely to find much support and could eventually drop to the September 1993 lows of $3.88, Jones said.
Elliott Wave International pegged support, basis Comex September silver, at $417.50, then $403.50 and $392.50.
At 0735 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.27/4.29, unchanged from Monday's New York close.
PLATINUM -
The market was shaky and could retest last week's lows of $394, with resistance at $410 and $420.
Prices were likely to head towards the May lows around $383.50, Jones said.
At 0735 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $401.00/404.00, down $1.50 from Monday's New York close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
